h1: The 6 Best USB4 NVMe SSD Enclosures Under $150, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best USB4 NVMe Enclosures: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 USB4 NVMe enclosures under $150 compared on controller chip, cooling, drive sizes, warranty and real speed limits.
summary: The ACASIS TBU405 Pro is the USB4 NVMe enclosure to buy if you edit video on a Mac and want a certified Intel Thunderbolt chip, and the SABRENT EC-U4TN is the best match for a fast Gen4 drive. The Satechi Pro suits very large SSDs, the Lexar E750 is the pick for a recognized brand's warranty, and the Cable Matters is the cheap way in.
intro: The 40Gbps number on the box is the first thing to distrust. It is the speed of the link, not the speed of your drive, and the real ceiling for a USB4 enclosure sits well below it because NVMe traffic is tunneled through the cable. If you buy an enclosure for the headline figure, you will be disappointed. Buy it for the controller, the heat management and the drive sizes it accepts.

We reviewed six USB4 and Thunderbolt-class enclosures from their listings and spec sheets, ranking them by controller chip, cooling approach, supported M.2 lengths and capacities, warranty and price. Where a listing leaves out a figure, we say so instead of guessing. Price buckets replace exact prices, and every enclosure here falls well under $150.

products.name: ACASIS 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure with Cooling Fan (TBU405 Pro)
products.verdict: A certified Intel JHL7440 chip, an active fan and listed testing on M1, M2 and M3 Macs and iPad Pro.
products.description:
The TBU405 Pro uses a certified Intel JHL7440 chip, an active cooling fan with a manual switch, and the listing says it has been tested with M1, M2 and M3 Macs and the iPad Pro. The Intel part is the point: it is a true Thunderbolt controller rather than a third-party USB4 bridge.

It takes first place because Mac users, who see the most trouble with unusual enclosure controllers, have the best reason to prefer a certified Intel chip. The fan helps hold speed on long transfers such as a multi-gigabyte video export, and the manual switch lets you turn it off for quiet work. The compromises are fan noise when it runs, and a listing that does not mention a long warranty.

Buy it if you edit video or move big project files on a Mac and want a Thunderbolt-certified chip. Skip it if you want a silent passive enclosure.

products.name: SABRENT USB4 NVMe SSD Enclosure (EC-U4TN)
products.verdict: 3,900MB/s over USB4 and 2,700MB/s over Thunderbolt, cooled by a fan, for PCIe NVMe only.
products.description:
The EC-U4TN lists 3,900MB/s over USB4 and 2,700MB/s over Thunderbolt, with an integrated active cooling fan. It accepts PCIe NVMe drives only, with no SATA M.2 support.

It ranks second because it states both its USB4 and Thunderbolt numbers, which is honest and useful: a Thunderbolt port will run slower than a USB4 port on this enclosure. That makes it a good partner for a fast PCIe Gen4 drive on a modern PC, where the 3,900MB/s figure applies. The narrow focus is the downside, since an older SATA M.2 drive simply will not work in it.

Buy it if you own a Gen4 NVMe SSD and a USB4 port, and want the most speed available at this price. Check that your SSD is NVMe and not SATA before ordering.
products.idealFor: Owners of a fast Gen4 NVMe SSD with a USB4 port.
products.skipIf: You have a SATA M.2 drive.

products.name: Satechi USB4 NVMe SSD Pro Enclosure
products.verdict: Up to 16TB, up to 3,840MB/s, a full accessory bundle and a 2-year warranty.
products.description:
The Satechi Pro supports drives up to 16TB in 2230 to 2280 lengths, over PCIe Gen 4 by 4 at up to 3,840MB/s. It comes with a full accessory bundle and a 2-year limited warranty.

It ranks third because the capacity ceiling and the bundle are unique in this group. If you are shopping for a 10TB class drive, many enclosures are not rated for it, and Satechi lists 16TB outright. A named brand with a stated 2-year warranty also gives you somewhere to go if a unit fails. It trails the Sabrent only on the cooling story, since the listing does not highlight active cooling.

Buy it if you use very large SSDs and want a documented warranty with a complete accessory kit. Expect heat on long transfers if there is no active fan.
products.idealFor: Users running a 10TB or larger SSD.
products.skipIf: You want an active fan for long transfers.

products.name: Lexar E750 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure
products.verdict: An aircraft-grade aluminum body, Thunderbolt 4 tested, 3800MB/s rated and a 2-year warranty.
products.description:
The E750 has an aluminum body that the listing calls aircraft-grade, a rated speed of up to 3800MB/s, Thunderbolt 4 testing and a 2-year limited warranty. Lexar is a known storage brand, which matters when you need support.

It ranks fourth because it gets the brand and warranty right, and loses ground on documentation: the listing gives no controller name and no drive-length support in the summary. An aluminum shell conducts heat out of the SSD without a fan, so it stays quiet, but a passive design can throttle on very long transfers.

Buy it if you want a quiet enclosure from a recognized maker with a clear warranty. Choose a fan-cooled model instead if you copy hundreds of gigabytes in one go.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want brand support and silence.
products.skipIf: You copy huge files for hours at a stretch.

products.name: Rosewill 40Gbps M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure
products.verdict: An ASM2464PD controller rated for up to 4 hours of full-speed use and drives up to 8TB.
products.description:
The Rosewill uses the ASM2464PD controller, is rated for up to 4 hours of full-speed use, and supports drives up to 8TB in 2230 to 2280 lengths. The four-hour claim is the unusual one, since most listings say nothing about sustained speed.

It ranks fifth because ASM2464PD is a well-known USB4 bridge chip, but the brand has a lower profile in storage than Lexar or Sabrent. The sustained-use rating is promising for long backups and large project archives. Treat it as a rated figure, not a measured result, and remember that real speed also depends on the SSD inside.

Buy it if you run multi-hour transfers and care more about endurance than a brand name. Check the return window in case your drive and controller do not get along.
pros: Rated for 4 hours at full speed
cons: Sustained rating is a seller figure
products.idealFor: Long backups and big project archives.
products.skipIf: You want a major storage brand's warranty.

products.name: Cable Matters 40Gbps USB4 / Thunderbolt 4 SSD Enclosure
products.verdict: The cheapest 40Gbps option here, with a temperature-controlled fan but single-sided SSDs only.
products.description:
The Cable Matters enclosure uses an ASM-class controller rated at 40Gbps, with an active temperature-controlled fan. It accepts single-sided M.2 drives only, up to 2280, and sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It ranks last because the single-sided limitation is a real catch. Many high-capacity SSDs use chips on both sides of the board, and those will not fit. If your drive is 1TB or 2TB single-sided, it works well and costs very little. The temperature-controlled fan only runs when needed, which is a smarter design than a fan that spins constantly.

Buy it if you have a standard single-sided drive and want the cheapest way into 40Gbps. Check that your SSD is single-sided before you order.
products.idealFor: Budget builders with a single-sided SSD.
products.skipIf: Your SSD has chips on both sides.

whatMatters.detail: The bridge chip translates between USB4 and the drive, and it decides which hosts and drives work well. A certified Intel part is the safest on Macs, while ASM-class chips are common and fast. Look for the chip name on the listing, and treat a missing name as a warning.

The link speed is 40Gbps, but tunneled NVMe throughput lands closer to 3,000 to 4,000MB/s on the best enclosures, and slower on Thunderbolt ports in some designs. The SABRENT lists 3,900MB/s on USB4 and 2,700MB/s on Thunderbolt. Prefer listings that give real MB/s figures.

Fast SSDs run hot, and a drive that overheats slows itself down. Fans keep speed up on long copies, aluminum bodies conduct heat quietly, and a thin plastic shell does neither. If you move large files, favor a fan or an aluminum body.

Check the supported lengths (2230 to 2280), whether the enclosure takes single-sided drives only, and whether it accepts SATA M.2 at all. Some listings, like the SABRENT, take PCIe NVMe only. A drive that does not fit is the most common return.
A 2-year limited warranty, as on the Lexar and Satechi, is a reasonable baseline. Check that a quality 40Gbps cable is included, since a cheap cable can quietly cut speeds to USB 3 levels.

faq.q: Will a USB4 enclosure work on a Thunderbolt 4 laptop?
faq.a: Yes. USB4 and Thunderbolt 4 share the same connector, and the enclosures here work on either. Speeds can differ by port, as the SABRENT listing shows with 3,900MB/s over USB4 and 2,700MB/s over Thunderbolt.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying an NVMe enclosure?
faq.a: Buying one that does not fit the drive. A SATA M.2 drive will not work in a PCIe NVMe enclosure, and a double-sided drive will not fit the Cable Matters. Check the drive type and sides before ordering.

faq.q: Is the ACASIS worth it over the Cable Matters?
faq.a: If you use a Mac or move large files, yes. The ACASIS has a certified Intel chip and Mac testing, while the Cable Matters is limited to single-sided SSDs. For a basic single-sided drive and occasional transfers, the cheaper one is fine.

Open the case, slide the SSD into the M.2 slot, fix it with the screw or latch, close the case and plug it in. Most take five minutes with no tools beyond the supplied screwdriver. A new drive needs formatting.

faq.q: Why is my enclosure slower than advertised?
faq.a: The 40Gbps number is the link rate, not the drive speed. A slow SSD, a poor cable, a USB 3 port or heat throttling can all cut the result. Use the included cable and a USB4 or Thunderbolt port.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about heat?
faq.a: On long transfers, yes. Fast SSDs get hot and slow themselves down. A fan, as on the ACASIS and SABRENT, or an aluminum shell, as on the Lexar, helps. Avoid leaving the enclosure on soft surfaces.

finalTake: For Mac creators, the ACASIS TBU405 Pro is the best USB4 NVMe enclosure here, with a certified Intel chip and an active fan. The SABRENT EC-U4TN is the pick for a fast Gen4 drive, the Satechi Pro handles the biggest SSDs, and the Lexar E750 offers brand support in a quiet aluminum body. The Cable Matters is the budget entry, but only for single-sided drives. Check your drive before your cart.
